vascular inflammation and endothelial cell dysfunction, as measured by circulating levels of sICM-1 and sVCM-1, are associated with the development of hypertension and arterial stiffening in type 1 diabetic individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vascular inflammation and endothelial function are involved in the development of arterial stiffening and, subsequently, of hypertension in type 2 diabetes.
the biomarkers we studied may have a role to play as early predictors of pulse pressure, and possibly also hypertension, in type 1 diabetic individuals.
the development of hypertension in type 2 diabetes is a complex process involving many factors and that the use of a single biomarker is unlikely to be helpful.
